transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-25 | Start: 15:30 UTC | Duration: ~63m
Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Daniel Cho (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (Aurora, Head of ML), Liam O'Connor (Platform), Hannah Wu (Security), Ethan Brooks (Product)
Recording: yes | Auto-transcription (medium quality)
Agenda: quick intro; success criteria; workload sizing; hosting tradeoffs (hosted vs dedicated vs private); benchmark plan; next steps

Summary (auto): customer evaluating deployment mode for POC. Primary concerns: latency SLOs for 95th/99th, cost per inference at scale, data residency and KMS, and ease of rollout. Action items and benchmark window agreed.

Transcript:
[00:00] Sofia (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. quick round of intros and then dive into what you need for the POC.
[00:12] Maya (Aurora): Hi, Maya here. We're trying to pick hosting for a 6-week POC to validate inference latency and cost for our routing assistant.
[00:22] Liam (Aurora): Liam, platform. we'll need to see how the inference nodes sit behind our edge, we currently run in GCP europe-west.
[00:30] Sofia: Perfect. Daniel's gonna do the deep infra questions.
[00:33] Daniel (Redwood SE): Hey all. quick note on my side: I'll ask about request shapes, concurrency, KV cache patterns, and what your current SLOs look like.
[00:45] Hannah (Aurora): And from security, we're worried about key management and audit logs. we have a strict policy about customer-managed keys, and any external host needs SOC2 + ISO.
[01:05] Daniel: Got it. just to calibrate — when you say routing assistant, are we doing multi-turn chat or a single-shot generation per request?
[01:12] Maya: Mostly single-shot but with an in-line context of ~150 tokens, sometimes 350 for extended context.
[01:20] Ethan (Aurora): Also want to note we have bursts during end-of-day planning windows, spikes up to 350 QPS for short periods. average steady QPS is around 45-60.
[01:35] Sofia: That's really helpful. sounds like you care about p99 latency under 300ms for the majority of requests?
[01:40] Maya: Right. p95 under 150ms ideally, p99 under 300ms. cost target is the other side — ideally we don't exceed our budgeted per-inference cost.
[01:50] Daniel: OK so this is the classic tradeoff: Hosted gives fastest time-to-value, Redwood Dedicated gives predictable throughput and latency, and Redwood Private gives you control for KMS and VPC but adds ops overhead.
[02:05] Maya: Can you give rough numbers? like, if we run a small model vs a large one, how does cost/latency behave on each mode?
[02:12] Sofia: Sure. rough back-of-envelope: Hosted per-token is highest unit price but no infra commit; Dedicated amortizes GPU cost so unit cost drops at higher QPS; Private has similar economics to Dedicated but add ops/maintenance. we'll send a TCO sheet.
[02:30] Liam: For Dedicated, how do autoscale and burst capacity work? we can't have sustained overcommit.
[02:36] Daniel: Dedicated supports reserve pools with configurable autoscale and burst. in practice you set a base capacity for steady QPS and allow burst nodes for short windows — there's a buffer for a few minutes while new instances spin up.
[02:50] Maya: Any folks running in-region? we have EU data residency requirements, so we'd prefer europe-west serving.
[02:56] Sofia: We can pin region on Hosted, deploy Dedicated in eu-west, or do Private on-prem if needed. note though that Private requires install and a short validation period.
[03:12] Hannah: About KMS — can you support customer-managed keys and HSM integration?
[03:18] Daniel: Yes. Private supports KMS/HSM integrations; Dedicated supports KMS via our key-wrapping integration, and Hosted can do envelope encryption but customers often prefer Dedicated/Private for full KMS control. there may be some nuance around audit export.
[03:36] Ethan: On benchmarks, what do you recommend we run to hit our p95/p99 targets?
[03:40] Daniel: We'll do a mix: cold-start traces, steady-state concurrency at 60 QPS, and a spike test to 350 QPS for 10 minutes. include realistic prompt distribution and KV cache enabled/disabled runs.
[03:55] Maya: How do you simulate KV cache? our workload benefits a lot from prefix caching.
[03:59] Daniel: We'll include a KV cache warm-up phase, and we can instrument cache hit rates. sometimes the transcriber writes KV cache as K V cash — sorry bad auto-text.
[04:12] Sofia: (laughs) noted.
[04:18] Liam: Any SLA differences between Hosted and Dedicated?
[04:22] Sofia: Hosted has standard uptime numbers but not the same SLA as Dedicated. Dedicated comes with committed SLOs and credits, which is why enterprises like it.
[04:30] Hannah: For compliance we need audit logs retention for at least 12 months, and granular RBAC. can Redwood support that out of the box?
[04:38] Daniel: Yes, we expose request-level logs with redaction options, and RBAC can be scoped at team and token levels. retention length and export can be configured for Dedicated/Private.
[04:52] Maya: Do you have customers who've chosen Hosted then moved to Dedicated? what's the friction?
[04:58] Sofia: Yep, pretty common. we do model pinning and rollout controls so the application layer rarely needs to change. network whitelisting and some IAM glue is usual work. it tends to be a few days of config plus a short validation rollout.
[05:12] Ethan: How much effort to run a short Private deployment? we might consider air-gap for some customers.
[05:18] Daniel: Private is heavier: you'll need infra for GPU machines, networking, and we'll coordinate the install. for a POC we can do a trimmed Private with a few nodes but expect ~4-6 week lead time for fully-validated on-prem.
[05:35] Maya: That timescale could be too long for our 6-week POC, so we may prefer Hosted or Dedicated for initial validation.
[05:42] Sofia: Makes sense. we can do a two-step POC: quick hosted baseline to validate quality and latency, then run Dedicated or Private benchmark if results show scale concerns.
[05:55] Liam: On the hosted baseline, what visibility do we get into kernel selection/quantization profiles?
[06:00] Daniel: We provide model config metadata: quantization level, memory profiles, and per-request token breakdown. Kernel-level details are abstracted but we publish performance profiles.
[06:14] Maya: We also need to measure cold-start p99 across 1v1 instances. how do you reproduce cold starts in hosted mode?
[06:20] Daniel: We'll orchestrate a staggered spike pattern and measure the first request tail latency; plus a cache-cold run where KV cache is cleared.
[06:30] Sofia: Let's talk benchmarks and timeline — propose: this week you share prompt sets and traces (Maya, Liam), next week we run hosted baseline, week after we do Dedicated window if needed. does that align?
[06:43] Maya: Yes, that aligns with our internal timeline.
[06:47] Ethan: If hosted shows we can meet p95 but not p99, what's the typical uplift in Dedicated?
[06:54] Daniel: Usually Dedicated reduces p99 by 20–40% in noisy neighbor scenarios due to isolated pools and fine-grained autoscale. caches help more for repeated prompts.
[07:08] Hannah: Encryption at rest — is that supported across all modes?
[07:12] Daniel: Yes; Hosted uses provider-managed keys by default with envelope encryption; Dedicated can integrate with your KMS, and Private gives you full control.
[07:25] Sofia: ok quick pause, any blockers we haven't covered?
[07:28] Maya: billing model — do you do monthly committed spend for Dedicated?
[07:33] Sofia: Yes, Dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly/annual commits. we can show a sliding scale of unit cost versus committed QPS.
[07:44] Liam: about network egress: can we peer VPC for Dedicated?
[07:49] Daniel: Yes, VPC peering and private link style connections supported. for Hosted you can do IP allowlisting and VPN tunnels for secure traffic.
[07:58] Maya: Are there any limitations with model sizes on Dedicated? we use a 70B model variant for some heavy rerank tasks.
[08:04] Daniel: We support multi-GPU for larger models in Dedicated and Private; Hosted has selected sizes in the catalog but we can bring larger models via dedicated pools. size will affect latency.
[08:22] Ethan: Let's detail the success criteria. from our side:
[08:26] Ethan: 1) p95 < 150ms, p99 < 300ms (as discussed)
[08:30] Ethan: 2) cost per inference below $0.0009 for our median prompt length
[08:34] Ethan: 3) audit logs and KMS controls validated
[08:37] Maya: add 4) seamless rollback if model quality regresses during rollout
[08:40] Daniel: we have canary rollouts and automatic fallback to smaller model variants. we'll include in the runbook.
[08:48] Sofia: great. i'll include those as success criteria in the summary doc.
[08:53] (small cross talk)
[09:05] Daniel: on the benchmarking plan — do you want us to run both hosted and dedicated in parallel windows to compare directly?
[09:12] Maya: yes if it's possible, that'd be ideal.
[09:16] Sofia: we can allocate a dedicated reserved pool for your runs; I'll need a commit for a short reserved window for the Dedicated test, or we can spin up a temporary pool that's metered.
[09:29] Liam: cost of temporary pool? we need to know if it's a big hit to run a 2-hour dedicated test.
[09:34] Sofia: temporary pools are billed at a slightly higher rate than reserved, but still predictable. we'll show estimates in the TCO and label the bench cost.
[09:45] Maya: On the hosted baseline, how do we ensure reproducibility? can you provide the exact model version and seed?
[09:52] Daniel: Yes, we can pin model version and include deterministic seeding where supported. also we can export the exact request traces.
[10:02] Hannah: about logging — redaction for PII is mandatory. can you redact on ingest or is it post-processing?
[10:09] Daniel: Both options exist. we can do pre-ingest redaction rules or redact in logs post-capture. we'll provide patterns and examples.
[10:20] Ethan: Ok let's capture the benchmark metrics we want: p50, p95, p99 latencies, error rates, QPS, CPU/GPU utilization, KV cache hit rate, and cost per 1k requests.
[10:33] Sofia: noted. we'll map these to visuals in the output deck.
[10:36] (brief silence)
[10:50] Maya: Are there any regulatory pitfalls with Hosted that would disqualify it for EU data residency?
[10:56] Daniel: Hosted can be pinned to EU regions and we provide data segregation controls, but some customers insist on Private if they need on-prem data residency or need certain certifications that we only provide with Private deployments.
[11:12] Liam: For the POC, we prefer not to do full Private. we'll do hosted baseline then Dedicated.
[11:18] Sofia: makes sense. we'll draft a plan: Week 0 (this week) — share artifacts; Week 1 — hosted baseline runs; Week 2 — Dedicated window and analysis; Week 3 — decision and potential pilot signoff.
[11:34] Ethan: timeline is tight but doable.
[11:38] Maya: one more question: if the hosted baseline shows model quality issues vs our golden set, would you recommend different quantization or model variant?
[11:46] Daniel: yes, we have quantization profiles and model variants that trade accuracy vs latency. Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization and batching settings tied to your eval set.
[11:58] Sofia: ok wrapping up. i'll send a short recap and include the TCO spreadsheet, security doc, and a proposed benchmark script.
[12:06] Maya: thanks. we'll send the prompt sets and traces by end of week.
[12:12] Hannah: security will review SOC2 docs and follow up on KMS questions.
[12:18] Sofia: thanks everyone. next call, we'll review results.
[12:22] (meeting ends)

End of transcript.
notes: Benchmarks to include cold-start, steady-state, and spike tests. Customer leans Hosted->Dedicated path due to POC timeline. Security wants KMS/ audit doc. Action items recorded.
